candidate_relations.reason: Pulsatile bleeding from the right ureteral orifice was treated with renal-artery embolization, but no renal-artery aneurysm is described.
Pyelonephritis does not explain pulsatile arterial bleeding from the ureteral orifice after stent removal.
Ureteroarterial fistula is the same diagnostic object as the reference and matches pulsatile arterial bleeding from the right ureteral orifice.
Remote treated rectal cancer is background history; the hemorrhage is from an arterial-ureteral communication, not tumor bleeding.
Cystoscopy localized pulsatile bleeding to the ureteral orifice rather than radiation injury of the bladder mucosa.
Radiation-induced hemorrhagic cystitis is a bladder-mucosal process, whereas bleeding issued from the ureter after stent extraction.
No pseudoaneurysm is documented; the index event is an arterial-ureteral fistula.
Nephrolithiasis is not described and would not produce pulsatile arterial ureteral bleeding.
Vascular disease is a compatible parent category but lacks the required ureteroarterial fistula specificity.
Rectal cancer recurrence is not shown; hematuria followed chronic stenting and arterial-ureteral communication.
Retrograde ureterography found a ureteroileal fistula, an associated enteric fistula rather than the arterial source of pulsatile right-sided bleeding.
No renal mass suggesting renal cell carcinoma is described.
Creatinine elevation and hydronephrosis reflect associated kidney injury, not the fistula causing hemorrhage.
Candida glabrata pelvic abscess after stent occlusion is a predisposing prior infection, not the acute bleeding diagnosis.
Infectious disease is a nonspecific label and is not the ureteroarterial fistula.
Bilateral ureteral strictures with chronic stents are a risk factor for ureteroarterial fistula, not the fistula itself.
Ureteroenteric fistula is the associated left-sided finding, not the arterial-ureteral communication causing massive hematuria.
Renal-vein thrombosis is not described and would not produce pulsatile ureteral arterial bleeding.
Arteriovenous fistula is a related vascular fistula but pairs artery with vein rather than ureter with artery.
Prior Candida glabrata infection is historical context, not the diagnosis of ureteroarterial fistula.

case_quality_flags: concurrent left ureteroileal fistula also documented
